# 受管 RPi-ImmortalWrt

`rpi-immortalwrt` 將節點、群組、規則、Selector 切換與區網裝置觀測交給
RPi-ImmortalWrt 專案的 broker。安裝、網路、安全防火牆、Nikki 生命週期與回復
仍由該專案管理。使用前須已完成該專案的嚴格 SSH、network／proxy 確認與私人 CA TLS controller 設定。

## 註冊與來源

先在本機建立 target。以下使用占位路徑與位址；controller、CA 與 SSH transport
必須和既有私人 connection JSON 一致。API secret 以既有 `0600` 私人檔案參照，
不要放入 TOML、命令列值或公開 YAML。

```sh
lazyclash targets add pi \
  --controller https://192.0.2.1:9090 \
  --ca-cert /absolute/RPi-ImmortalWrt/private/pki/ca.crt \
  --secret-file /absolute/RPi-ImmortalWrt/private/controller.secret \
  --rpi-project-dir /absolute/RPi-ImmortalWrt \
  --rpi-connection-file /absolute/RPi-ImmortalWrt/private/managed-pi.json
lazyclash --target pi configs source set --kind rpi-immortalwrt
lazyclash --target pi rules source set --kind rpi-immortalwrt
lazyclash --target pi --read-only
```

`targets edit pi` 也接受兩個 `--rpi-*` 旗標。設定會保存獨立的
`[targets.managed_rpi]`，包含絕對 `project_dir` 與 `connection_file`。兩個來源
只接受 `kind = "rpi-immortalwrt"`，不接受 generic binary、home 或 source path。
`configs source clear` 解除節點／群組來源後，受管 owner 邊界仍保留。

Broker 使用本機 `python3 PROJECT/scripts/device/proxy_manage.py`，由 connection JSON
執行專案的嚴格 SSH。連 API 前先核對 broker 的 controller、CA 與 SSH transport，
失配即停止。請用 `--target pi`；已知受管 endpoint 不接受臨時 `--controller`。
connection、broker snapshot 及 broker receipt 必須位於專案 `private/` 內，為
`0600`、單一 hard link、無 symlink 的普通檔案。

## 編輯、確認與回復

沿用既有節點／群組 UI 或 CLI，先預覽再以精確 digest 套用：

```sh
lazyclash --target pi proxies edit 'Node name' --interactive
lazyclash --target pi proxies import --file /absolute/private/nodes.yaml --json
lazyclash --target pi proxies import --file /absolute/private/nodes.yaml \
  --yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST --json
lazyclash --target pi rules add-domain example.com --via PROXY --json
lazyclash --target pi rules add-domain example.com --via PROXY \
  --yes --expect REVIEWED_DIGEST --json
```

预覽不停止 Nikki；套用完整 profile 變更可能暫停代理，broker 會顯示此影響並走
RPi-ImmortalWrt 的驗證、交易、嚴格 reconnect 確認與回復流程。預覽綁定 profile、
network、boot 與 core identity；context 改變須重新預覽。來源只有 `proxies`、
`proxy-groups` 與 `rules` 可編輯，controller 與網路設定仍由專案 owner 決定。

節點／群組操作使用 `configs verify RECEIPT_ID`、`configs restore RECEIPT_ID --yes`；
規則操作使用 `rules verify RECEIPT_ID`、`rules restore RECEIPT_ID --yes`。
遇到 `owner_result_unknown`，保留 receipt，先 verify，勿自動重送寫入。
Restore 直接交由 broker 核對與回復，不要求失敗後的 proxy 先恢復健康。
Lazyclash receipt 只參照 broker receipt，不另存完整私人 profile。

## 1. Why `lazyclash` fails to start

The code on `main` works fine. The problem is that the installed release is older than your settings file.

- Your `~/.config/lazyclash/config.toml` has a `windows-laptop` target with paths like `C:/Users/david/...`. A development build wrote those paths after v0.1.11.
- Windows path support arrived in three commits after the release (`ca29d68`, `f141234`, `3b00382`). All three are ahead of `origin/main` and no version has been tagged with them.
- The Homebrew v0.1.11 binary only accepts Unix-style absolute paths. At `internal/config/config.go:128` it rejects `C:/...`, and that one target stops the whole program from starting.
- `lazyclash upgrade` said "up-to-date" because Homebrew has nothing newer than v0.1.11. That part is working correctly.

I built the current `main` and ran it against your config: `lazyclash targets list` loads and shows all 6 targets, including `windows-laptop`.

**To fix it:**
- **Now:** run it from source with `go run ./cmd/lazyclash`.
- **Properly:** push and release v0.1.12. The three Windows commits have no `CHANGELOG.md` entries yet, so add those before tagging.

**A real weakness this exposes:** if the settings file contains one target that the binary can't parse, the whole program refuses to start. Every time the format gets a new feature, older binaries (for example on another machine) will hit this again. A better approach would be to skip the target it doesn't understand, show a warning, and still start. I can do that if you'd like.

## 2. Finishing the leftover changes

The uncommitted changes were the unfinished **managed RPi-ImmortalWrt** feature. It hands node, group and rule edits, and LAN device inventory, to the RPi-ImmortalWrt project's broker. The code and tests were done; it just hadn't been committed. (The session in `.specstory` is a different feature, routing topology, and that one was already committed.)

What I did to finish it:
- `go vet ./...` was clean and `go test ./...` all passed.
- Two files hadn't been run through `gofmt` (`internal/configwork/source.go`, `internal/rulework/service.go`), so I formatted them.
- Added an Unreleased entry to `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Committed as **`32be3e8` feat: delegate managed RPi-ImmortalWrt targets to the owner broker** (43 files).

I committed straight to `main` because the earlier commits were made the same way. Nothing has been pushed. The only files left uncommitted are the `.specstory/history/*.md` conversation logs, which the previous session also left untracked.

Transfer private helper requests over verified SFTP without relying on Windows shell stdin forwarding. Preserve existing SSH policy and bind lifecycle actions to the recorded user, paths, executables and task.

  lifecycle website probes get one bounded warmup retry with per-site evidence.
- Saved connectivity checks honor their full request budget.
- Added `rpi-immortalwrt` rule and node/group sources that hand edits, Selector
  switches and LAN device inventory to the RPi-ImmortalWrt project's broker.
  Targets keep a `[targets.managed_rpi]` owner boundary, reviewed digests,
  broker-referenced receipts and verify/restore; ad-hoc `--controller` access to
  a managed endpoint is refused.

## 0.1.11 — 2026-09-23

- Homebrew-owned `upgrade` now invokes the exact installed formula's owning
  `brew upgrade`, verifies the resulting stable executable and reports the
  actual version. Check mode previews without upgrading or requiring GitHub;
  pins, manager errors and unchanged formulas retain Homebrew's policy.

I haven't pushed or tagged anything. The release is ready locally, and there's one decision for you first.

## Release is ready locally
- **`cad72a6` chore(release): prepare v0.1.12**: adds the Windows, diagnostics and managed RPi entries to `CHANGELOG.md`, bumps the README version pin to `@v0.1.12`, and adds the two newly embedded PowerShell scripts to `scripts/distribution.json`.
- The same checks CI runs all pass: `test_release`, `test_distribution`, and `check-distribution.py`, which builds and smoke-tests the source tree and Go module from the committed revision. Cross-builds for Windows and linux/arm64 also succeed.
- Releasing needs the tag on `origin/main`: the workflow refuses a tag whose commit isn't on `origin/main`. So you have to push `main` first, then push the tag. Main is currently 7 commits ahead of `origin`.

## Are the two features finished?

**Windows: ready to release.**
- There are no TODO items or unfinished code paths.
- The commit messages say it was tested on real machines: Verge and background Mihomo deployments, cloning a target from a Windows source, a Verge restart, and connectivity checks.
- Your own `windows-laptop` target loads fine on `main`.

**Managed RPi: the lazyclash side is done, but the other half isn't committed.**
- Its tests pass, and the logs in `RPi-ImmortalWrt/private/proxy-manage/` show it has been used against the real device: 11 inspects, 7 profile runs and 1 selector switch.
- But the broker it calls lives in the RPi-ImmortalWrt repo, and that work is all uncommitted. `scripts/device/proxy_manage.py`, `management_transport.py`, `proxy_ui.py` and their tests are untracked, and that repo has 33 uncommitted changes in total.
- If v0.1.12 goes out now, the RPi feature still works for you, since your local copy of RPi-ImmortalWrt has the broker. But anyone following `docs/managed-rpi.md` would be pointed at a project that doesn't contain the broker yet.
- Your lazyclash config doesn't have an RPi target yet either.

My recommendation: commit the RPi-ImmortalWrt side first, then release v0.1.12 with both features. Your startup error is only fixed once v0.1.12 is on Homebrew, so if you want that sooner, you could release now and add a line in the changelog saying the RPi feature needs the not-yet-published broker.

When you decide, I can:
1. Wrap up and commit the RPi-ImmortalWrt work (I'd look through those 33 changes and run its tests first).
2. Push `main`, then create and push `v0.1.12` in the same style as `v0.1.11`: `git tag -a v0.1.12 -m "Release v0.1.12: …"` followed by `git push origin main v0.1.12`.

diff --git a/internal/config/preserve.go b/internal/config/preserve.go
index 2073057..dabd24e 100644
--- a/internal/config/preserve.go
+++ b/internal/config/preserve.go
@@ -242,6 +242,10 @@ func preserve(raw []byte, cfg Config) ([]byte, error) {
 		if err != nil {
 			return nil, err
 		}
+		b, err = patchManagedRPi(b, t.ManagedRPi)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
 		b, err = patchRuleSource(b, t.RuleSource)
 		if err != nil {
 			return nil, err
@@ -429,3 +433,44 @@ func patchPreferences(raw []byte, p TUIPreferences) ([]byte, error) {
 	}
 	return applyEdits(raw, []edit{{start, end, b}}), nil
 }
+
+func patchManagedRPi(raw []byte, source *ManagedRPi) ([]byte, error) {
+	exprs, err := expressions(raw)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	start, end := -1, len(raw)
+	for _, e := range exprs {
+		if e.kind == unstable.KeyValue && e.table == "targets" && e.key == "managed_rpi" {
+			return nil, errors.New("inline managed_rpi cannot be edited while preserving comments; use [targets.managed_rpi]")
+		}
+		if e.kind != unstable.Table && e.kind != unstable.ArrayTable {
+			continue
+		}
+		if start >= 0 {
+			end = e.start
+			break
+		}
+		if e.table == "targets.managed_rpi" {
+			start = e.start
+		}
+	}
+	if source == nil {
+		if start < 0 {
+			return raw, nil
+		}
+		return applyEdits(raw, []edit{{start, end, nil}}), nil
+	}
+	block := []byte("\n[targets.managed_rpi]\n")
+	if start >= 0 {
+		block = raw[start:end]
+	}
+	block, err = patchFields(block, "targets.managed_rpi", []field{{"project_dir", source.ProjectDir}, {"connection_file", source.ConnectionFile}})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if start < 0 {
+		return append(append(raw, '\n'), block...), nil
+	}
+	return applyEdits(raw, []edit{{start, end, block}}), nil
+}

	state := p.state
	p.state = nil
	if p != state.view {

	result.Formula, result.Path = p.Formula, p.StablePath
	if progress == nil {

	}

		return result, err

func runCommand(ctx context.Context, program string, args []string, progress io.Writer) (string, error) {
	query := len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "--cellar" || args[0] == "--prefix")
	if query {
		var cancel context.CancelFunc
		ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
	}
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, program, args...)
	configureCommand(cmd)
	if progress == nil {
		progress = io.Discard
	}
	var output limitedOutput
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = progress, progress
	if query {
		cmd.Stdout = &output
		for _, entry := range os.Environ() {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(entry, "HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=") {
				cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, entry)
			}
		}
		cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1")
	}
	err := cmd.Run()
	if ctx.Err() != nil {
		return "", ctx.Err()
	}
	return output.String(), err
}

type limitedOutput struct{ buffer bytes.Buffer }

func (w *limitedOutput) String() string { return w.buffer.String() }

func (w *limitedOutput) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
	if w.buffer.Len()+len(data) > 8192 {
		return 0, errors.New("Homebrew query output exceeds limit")
	}
	return w.buffer.Write(data)
}

package brewupgrade

import (
	"bytes"

func TestNativeFakeManagerArgvProgressAndCancellation(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "fake-brew")
	body := `#!/bin/sh
case "$1" in
  --cellar) printf '%s\n' "$HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE" "$#" "$2" ;;
  upgrade) printf 'stdout:%s:%s\n' "$#" "$2"; printf 'stderr progress\n' >&2 ;;
  sleep) exec sleep 30 ;;
  fail) exit 7 ;;
  --prefix) printf '%9000s' x ;;
esac
`
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var progress bytes.Buffer
	output, err := runCommand(context.Background(), path, []string{"--cellar", "acme/tools/installed-name"}, &progress)
	if err != nil || output != "1\n2\nacme/tools/installed-name\n" || progress.Len() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("query=%q progress=%q error=%v", output, progress.String(), err)
	}
	output, err = runCommand(context.Background(), path, []string{"upgrade", "acme/tools/installed-name"}, &progress)
	if err != nil || output != "" || !strings.Contains(progress.String(), "stdout:2:acme/tools/installed-name") || !strings.Contains(progress.String(), "stderr progress") {
		t.Fatalf("upgrade output=%q progress=%q error=%v", output, progress.String(), err)
	}
	if _, err := runCommand(context.Background(), path, []string{"fail"}, nil); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("nonzero manager status swallowed")
	}
	if _, err := runCommand(context.Background(), path, []string{"--prefix", "formula"}, nil); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("unbounded query output accepted")
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 50*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	start := time.Now()
	if _, err := runCommand(ctx, path, []string{"sleep"}, nil); !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("cancellation: %v", err)
	}
	if time.Since(start) > 2*time.Second {
		t.Fatal("cancellation did not stop manager promptly")
	}
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-23 06:33:10Z)**_

I've made both fixes and committed them as **`49bca79`**. Nothing is pushed yet, and the tap step needs a token from you before it does anything.

**1. `lazyclash upgrade` now refreshes Homebrew first.**
- When it runs `brew upgrade`, it sets `HOMEBREW_AUTO_UPDATE_SECS=0`, so Homebrew always pulls the latest tap and won't report a just-published version as "up-to-date".
- If you've set `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`, that still wins.
- The check-only query commands still skip the refresh, as before.
- I added a test for both cases, and noted the behaviour in the docs and the CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

**2. A release now asks the Homebrew tap to update right away.**
- After a release is published, `release.yml` starts the tap's update job for lazyclash (`sync.yml` in `homebrew-tap`).
- The tap's hourly schedule is heavily delayed by GitHub. The runs we saw were at 18:56, 22:12, 00:36 and 06:00, which is why v0.1.12 didn't show up on its own.
- The default token a workflow gets can't start a workflow in another repo, so this needs a secret, and it isn't set yet. Until it is, the step just leaves a notice and the release still succeeds. If starting the tap job fails, it only shows a warning, because the release is already out by then.

`actionlint` and the release tests pass, and so do `go vet` and `go test -count=1 ./...`.

**What you need to do** (I didn't create the token; putting your own `gh` login token into a repo secret would give that repo far more access than it needs):
1. On GitHub, create a fine-grained personal access token that can only access `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`, with the **Actions: Read and write** permission.
2. Run `! gh secret set HOMEBREW_TAP_DISPATCH_TOKEN -R daviddwlee84/lazyclash` and paste the token.

After that, say "push" and I'll push `main`. It doesn't need a new release; the change takes effect from the next release.

It isn't working yet: the secret never got saved. The GitHub API shows 0 Actions secrets and 0 environments on `lazyclash`, and `homebrew-tap` has no secrets or variables either. You may have created the token without finishing the secret step.

**To finish it on github.com:**
1. Open **daviddwlee84/lazyclash** → Settings → Secrets and variables → **Actions**.
2. Click **New repository secret**. Put it in the lazyclash repo, not homebrew-tap, and use the Actions tab (Dependabot and Codespaces secrets are separate lists).
3. Name it exactly `HOMEBREW_TAP_DISPATCH_TOKEN` and paste the token as the value. The token must be able to access `homebrew-tap`, with **Actions: Read and write**.

Once it's saved I can confirm it with `gh api`, though I can only see the name, not the value. To check that the token itself works, you can run this once yourself (the token then only lives in your terminal):
```
! GH_TOKEN=<your token> gh workflow run sync.yml -R daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap -f tool=lazyclash
```
If a new "Sync stable formulas" run starts in `homebrew-tap`, the permissions are right. I'd rather not test by re-running the release on v0.1.12: it would rebuild the files, and the publish script refuses to replace files that already exist, so it would stop before ever reaching the tap step.

**What's different from before**

| | Before (up to v0.1.12) | Now (`49bca79`) |
|---|---|---|
| After a release | The tap only got the new formula on its hourly schedule, which GitHub delays by hours (this time the gap was 3–6 hours) | The release workflow starts the tap update right after publishing, so the formula updates within minutes |
| `lazyclash upgrade` | If Homebrew had refreshed recently, it skipped refreshing the tap and reported "up-to-date" (what we saw this time) | It always refreshes the tap first (`HOMEBREW_AUTO_UPDATE_SECS=0`); `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` is still respected |

When each part takes effect:
- **The release change** only works after `main` is pushed and the secret is set. The next release will be the first to use it.
- **The `upgrade` change** only reaches your machine with the next release. The `lazyclash` you have installed now is v0.1.12, which still behaves the old way.

`49bca79` isn't pushed yet. Once the secret is set, say the word and I'll push and confirm the secret is there.

The step that can't be automated is creating the token. There's no need to apply for anything, but GitHub has no API for creating fine-grained personal access tokens, so that part has to be done on the website. Everything after that I can do for you.

**What your current token is used for**
- "Homebrew + Scoop" appears to be stored as secrets in two other repos: `translate` (`TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN`, used to publish the Scoop manifest) and `dev-cli` (`HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`).
- The `translate` release workflow also says Homebrew updates come only from the tap's hourly or manual update job. So all seven of your tools have the same delay we hit with lazyclash.
- GitHub never shows a token's value again after it's created, so I can't copy it out of those secrets into lazyclash.

**Two options**

1. **A new dedicated token (recommended).** It's the safest: its only permission is starting workflows in `homebrew-tap`.
   - On the Fine-grained tokens page shown in your screenshot, click **Generate new token**.
   - Set Repository access to only `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`, and Permissions → **Actions: Read and write**.
   - After it's generated, copy it and tell me. I'll run `pbpaste | gh secret set HOMEBREW_TAP_DISPATCH_TOKEN -R daviddwlee84/lazyclash`, which reads it straight from the clipboard without displaying it, then confirm the secret is there.

2. **Reuse "Homebrew + Scoop".** You can add **Actions: Read and write** to the existing token and its value stays the same. But I'd still need that value.
   - If you saved it somewhere, like a password manager, copy it and I'll set it the same way.
   - If you didn't save it, you'd have to regenerate it, which changes the value. The copies in `translate` and `dev-cli` would then need updating too. I can update all three secrets from the clipboard in one go, but any other place that uses the token would stop working.

Once the token works, I can add the same "start the tap update" step to your other tools' release workflows, so none of them wait on the hourly job again. Tell me which option you want and I'll set it up after you've copied the token.
